quality_scores.summary: A clean, well-structured introductory presentation on Google Cloud AI features with clear explanations and concise formatting, though it lacks quantitative metrics and deeper technical examples.

seven_cs_evaluation.Clear: The definitions and service descriptions are direct and easy to grasp for an audience of any technical level.
seven_cs_evaluation.Concise: Bullet points are kept brief and generally refrain from unnecessary fluff.
seven_cs_evaluation.Correct: Technical terminology and Google Cloud product naming are accurate.
seven_cs_evaluation.Complete: Covers key GCP AI offerings well, though it lacks implementation details or performance benchmarks.
seven_cs_evaluation.Concrete: Product references are specific (TPU, AutoML, Vision API), but real-world case studies or statistics are missing.
seven_cs_evaluation.Coherent: Logical flow from high-level definitions to infrastructure, build options, specialized APIs, and final summary.
seven_cs_evaluation.Courteous: Maintains an engaging, respectful, and audience-friendly professional tone.

strengths: Highly scannable bullet-point structure designed well for live presentations.
Translates complex machine learning concepts (e.g., Cloud TPUs, AutoML) into simple, accessible language.
Logical structure flowing from core definitions to custom development, pre-built APIs, and a clear summary slide.
issues_found: Lacks concrete performance data or real-world metrics (e.g., TPU speedup ratios or enterprise ROI examples).
Definitions are occasionally overly simplified (e.g., defining 'The Cloud' solely as Google tools).
Minor layout/formatting inconsistencies in heading titles (e.g., Slide 7 'API' placed on its own line).
recommendations: Add key quantitative metrics or enterprise case studies to support product capability claims.
Standardize slide header hierarchies across all slides for better visual consistency.
Include brief real-world industry use cases on capability slides (e.g., healthcare, retail, finance).

storytelling_analysis.feedback: The presentation functions well as a product feature catalog, but lacks a compelling narrative arc. It opens with a generic title and textbook definition rather than a captivating hook or problem statement (e.g., the difficulty/cost of building modern intelligent apps). The narrative jumps abruptly from general definitions in Slide 2 to specific hardware specs (Cloud TPU) in Slide 3, before explaining software building tools and specialized APIs. Reordering the presentation—moving from out-of-the-box perception APIs (Language, Vision, Translation) to custom building tools (AutoML, ML Engine) and finally to the underlying infrastructure (TPU)—creates a clearer progression from simple to advanced concepts. Lastly, the deck concludes abruptly with a summary and generic Q&A slide without a clear Call to Action (CTA) or forward-looking takeaway for the audience.
